text: Lessons 5 and 6 built a network in each cloud. This lesson puts a real VM into each one — azurerm_linux_virtual_machine into the Azure subnet, aws_instance into the AWS subnet — and that's where the two providers' resource shapes genuinely diverge, not just in naming.

In Azure's model, a VM never attaches to a subnet directly — it attaches to a network interface, and the NIC attaches to the subnet. azurerm_network_interface is its own resource, and its ip_configuration block sets subnet_id = azurerm_subnet.web.id, reaching back to the exact subnet Lesson 5 created, with the same implicit-dependency mechanics seen there — just one lesson further back in the chain.

azurerm_linux_virtual_machine takes the NIC's id inside network_interface_ids — a list, because Azure VMs can carry more than one NIC even though this one carries just one. size and admin_username are plain scalar arguments, while admin_ssh_key, os_disk, and source_image_reference are required nested blocks that round out what the resource needs before Terraform can actually boot anything.

aws_instance skips the separate network-interface resource entirely for this common case — subnet_id = aws_subnet.web.id attaches it straight to Lesson 6's subnet, no middle resource required. ami names the machine image to boot, instance_type is AWS's name for VM size, and associate_public_ip_address controls whether the instance gets a reachable public address at all.

This isn't arbitrary: Azure treats the network interface as a first-class, independently manageable resource you could detach and reattach elsewhere, or add several of to one VM. AWS creates an elastic network interface behind aws_instance automatically, and you'd only reach for an explicit aws_network_interface resource if a VM needed more than its one default NIC.

Next lesson combines everything built across Lessons 5 through 7 into a single configuration that declares both azurerm and aws together — one state file, one terraform apply, two clouds — plus the provider alias pattern for when one cloud alone needs more than one region or subscription.
